decisions.title: User Accounts Export contract

ownerDecision.basis: Explicit attached Resolve PEOPLE-09 export specification prerequisite request; owner-approved ProjectX specification instead of additional SevenRooms Export discovery.

decisions.rationale: Resolve the implementation specification gate without guessing reference behavior; minimize exported data and independently authorize current-Venue exports.

specification.source: Existing scoped PEOPLE-03 User Accounts roster domain; export must narrow its organization roster to current-Venue membership/access, not change or export the organization-wide read endpoint wholesale.
specification.filters: None in v1; complete authorized Venue roster, not the current UI filter/page

authorization.tenantAuthority: Trusted server authorization context only; no browser/client-selected Organization or Venue authority

specification.ordering: Ascending User UUID, matching deterministic PEOPLE-03 account ordering; not a SevenRooms ordering claim
specification.emptyRoster: Valid CSV with header row only
specification.formulaInjectionProtection: Neutralize exported text beginning with spreadsheet formula/control prefixes including =, +, -, @, tab and carriage return; CSV quoting alone is not the neutralization contract. ProjectX security decision; do not mutate stored fields.

audit.convention: Scoped export attempt/result using existing append-only, redacted audit conventions
audit.excluded: CSV contents and exported field values; no generated-file storage

specification.failureAtomicity: Complete generation before any CSV response; no partial CSV response/file on failure
specification.frontendBoundary: PEOPLE-09B remains separate; no frontend implementation in this specification task

decisions.notes: Specification prerequisite satisfied only. PEOPLE-09 READY, not VERIFIED; canonical capability registration, least-privilege RLS/read seam, audit and API implementation/tests belong to PEOPLE-09. No runtime, migrations, generated contracts or reference classifications changed.

decisions.title: Export-only durable audit write seam

ownerDecision.option: Option A — narrow export-only writer inside PEOPLE-09
ownerDecision.basis: Explicit attached Record owner-approved PEOPLE-D010 request; documentation/architecture decision only, not implementation or publication approval.

decisions.rationale: Existing name-mutation history writers cannot persist export attempt/results; authorize a narrow export-only metadata writer and transaction seam without a generic audit subsystem or wider data authority.

mayIntroduce: PEOPLE-09-specific trusted-scope transaction seam for durable success, denied and failed results
Separate denial/failure audit durability from rolled-back export work where required

auditContract.exportedRowCount: Nullable; permitted only for result=success; required success record includes the exported row count, including zero
auditContract.immutability: Repository-consistent immutable history mechanism; no mutation of historical entries
auditContract.runtimeAuditRead: No broad SELECT access; any runtime audit readability requires a separate explicit authorization decision

writer.inputValidation: Explicit validation, fixed table/event and result/row-count constraints; no generic SQL execution

auditContract.trustedContext: Derive/validate actor, Organization, Venue and request ID from trusted server-established request/transaction context. Unavoidable parameters must match that context and referential ownership; browser DTOs and custom settings alone are not identity/tenant proof.
auditContract.referentialValidation: Actor User and Organization exist; Venue exists and belongs to Organization. Follow composite tenant ownership conventions. Actor UUID is attribution, not employee/name ownership; if following existing history's lack of User FK, explicitly validate User existence in the writer and document that safe alternative without inventing deletion/lifecycle semantics.
auditContract.denied: Trusted resolver establishes actor/Organization/Venue/request context before capability evaluation. Durably record denied through the narrow writer without requiring people.accounts.export merely to audit denial; validate attribution/scope to prevent cross-tenant injection. Grant no roster visibility and run no export query after denial. Never fabricate missing trusted context.
auditContract.failed: Roll back authorized export work; safely classify failure and persist a separate bounded failed audit record through the export-only seam, without failure internals, partial CSV or resurrecting/committing rolled-back work.
auditContract.success: Required success audit with exported row count persists before successful CSV response. If audit persistence fails, fail the response; no successful CSV without required audit and no exported values stored.
auditContract.failureAtomicity: PEOPLE-D009 remains authoritative for no partial CSV; PEOPLE-D010 supplies the durable audit seam, including success audit before response and independent denial/failure durability. Row ID and request correlation are explicitly approved minimal persistence metadata, not added exported CSV fields.
auditContract.identityAndModuleBoundary: No employee inference, Booked By/Server Names coupling, tenant visibility widening, arbitrary actor/scope/event injection or runtime audit-read API

futureImplementation: Forward-only migration without historical migration edits
Export-specific audit table/writer and tightly scoped application helper

unresolvedQuestions.question: Which independently designed deployment and hosting model should ProjectX use for the first production milestone?
unresolvedQuestions.whyItMatters: Deployment model and hosting account shape operating cost, recovery, and how many moving parts every small task must verify.
projectEvidence: 16 mapped product modules; 144 screens; reservation, availability and client journeys cross module boundaries.
No evidence of reference deployment topology or cloud provider.
unresolvedQuestions.whyRecommended: The visible flows have strong cross-module transactions and no measured need for distributed deployment. Hosting provider remains a separate selection after requirements and cost approval.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Which frontend/backend/runtime and repository combination should be the starting implementation contract?
unresolvedQuestions.whyItMatters: The stack determines developer workflow, shared contracts, deployment toolchain and the cost of changing frameworks later.
projectEvidence: 144 screens with editable forms, calendar, floorplan and nested panels; 16 modules intended as small independently verifiable tasks.
No reference framework, language or repository structure is observable.
unresolvedQuestions.whyRecommended: Form-heavy web UI and many bounded tasks benefit from an explicit typed client/API seam and one reviewable repository; no stack is inferred from SevenRooms.
unresolvedQuestions.whatBecomesHarderToChangeLater: Framework-specific UI components, backend libraries, build scripts and cross-repo contracts.

unresolvedQuestions.question: What data store and account/organization/venue isolation model should ProjectX enforce?
unresolvedQuestions.whyItMatters: Tenant hierarchy and isolation determine every data key, authorization query, backup scope and the consequences of an access bug.
projectEvidence: Venue selector; user form mentions the same access at other venues; venue-scoped routes; reservation links to client, shift, area and table.
The exact account→organization→venue hierarchy and cross-venue sharing semantics are UNKNOWN.
unresolvedQuestions.whyRecommended: Observed relationships and reservation concurrency call for transactions and explicit scoped queries. The hierarchy and client-sharing rules must be confirmed before finalizing keys.
unresolvedQuestions.whatBecomesHarderToChangeLater: Tenant keys, foreign keys, policy coverage and migration/backup model.

unresolvedQuestions.question: How should users authenticate, hold sessions, and receive venue-scoped privileges?
unresolvedQuestions.whyItMatters: The account exposes guest PII, payment-related controls and cross-venue access; credential ownership and permission scope are security boundaries.
projectEvidence: User Accounts displays access levels, granular permissions, MFA option and multi-venue assignment; only one account role was observed.
Alternate-role authorization and actual sign-in/session semantics remain UNKNOWN.
unresolvedQuestions.whyRecommended: It separates identity proofing from app-owned, per-object and per-venue authorization and avoids storing passwords in the first milestone.
unresolvedQuestions.whatBecomesHarderToChangeLater: User identity IDs, session migration and permission vocabulary.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Which API style and validation/contract authority should connect the web client and domain modules?
unresolvedQuestions.whyItMatters: Contract shape controls independent task ownership, integration verification and future client compatibility.
projectEvidence: Many form fields, sortable lists, calendars and state changes; no reference API implementation or schema is evidenced.
Roadmap requires focused API contract tests for each module.
unresolvedQuestions.whyRecommended: It offers explicit versioned, testable boundaries and reduces the chance that one screen change forces broad module edits.
unresolvedQuestions.whatBecomesHarderToChangeLater: Client SDK, pagination, errors, version policy and integration contracts.

unresolvedQuestions.question: What production recovery target and environment/CI spending envelope should guide infrastructure design?
unresolvedQuestions.whyItMatters: Reservation operations can affect active service; recovery expectations determine backup frequency, restore rehearsal and staging cost.
projectEvidence: The product handles reservations, clients and operational shift settings, but no traffic, budget, RPO, RTO or regulatory retention target is documented.
Production write behavior has not been tested.
unresolvedQuestions.whyRecommended: Live reservations warrant a recoverable staging-to-production process, while no evidence justifies high-availability infrastructure yet. Targets are recommendations, not guarantees.
unresolvedQuestions.whatBecomesHarderToChangeLater: Backup design, hosting tiers, restore process and recurring cost.
